clinician.final_diagnosis: K. pneumoniae endogenous endophthalmitis with wide retinal necrosis in a previously healthy subject
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 72-year-old immunocompetent male presented with acute prostatitis and was found to have ampicillin-resistant K. pneumoniae urinary infection. He developed right eye floaters and vision loss 3 days after admission. Ophthalmologic evaluation revealed severe anterior chamber inflammation, fibrin, poorly dilated pupil, and vitreous abscess on ultrasound indicating endogenous endophthalmitis. Despite topical corticosteroid and cycloplegic therapy with little benefit, the patient underwent urgent pars plana vitrectomy and vitreous biopsy with intravitreal vancomycin and ceftazidime injection. Intraoperative findings showed a moderately ischemic retina with vasculitis and an area of infiltrated retina temporal to the central fovea, consistent with wide retinal necrosis. Although microbiological culture or PCR of vitreous biopsy was not documented in the available data, the clinical temporal correlation between initial K. pneumoniae urinary infection and ocular findings, plus the intraoperative retinal pathology, supports the diagnosis.
